title: Build apartments and commercial buildings to the building code (NCC Volume One)
what: As a licensed builder, carry out building work on Class 2 to 9 buildings so that the building complies with the building code: the Building Code of Australia (NCC Volume One) with the ACT Appendix. The edition in force is NCC 2025 since 1 May 2026, with a 12-month transition. The ACT's variations are in the ACT Appendix on the ACT Legislation Register, not counted here.

sources.title: Building Act 2004 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 49(2) (current republication (R57, from 10 November 2026; Building Act 2004 | Acts))
sources.quote: (2) A person commits an offence if— (a) the person is a licensed builder; and (b) the person carries out building work; and (c) the building work does not, or will not, result in a building that complies with the building code.

sources.title: Building Act 2004 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 136(1) (current republication (R57, from 10 November 2026; Building Act 2004 | Acts))
sources.quote: 136 Building code (1) In this Act: building code means— (a) the Building Code of Australia prepared and published by the Australian Building Codes Board as amended from time to time by— (i) the Australian Building Codes Board; and (ii) the Australian Capital Territory Appendix to the Building Code of Australia; and (b) a document prescribed by regulation.

sources.title: Building Act 2004 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 30(1), words naming the body (found 27 Nov 2026) (current republication (R57, from 10 November 2026; Building Act 2004 | Acts))
sources.quote: 30 When building approvals not to be issued—general (1) A certifier must not issue a building approval if carrying out the site work to which the application for the approval relates would result in the contravention of this Act or any other law in force in the ACT

triggers.note: when carrying out building work on a Class 2 to 9 building (apartments, hotels, offices, shops, factories, warehouses, car parks, public buildings)

reach.note: Volume One covers Class 2 to 9 buildings. Builders in other classes (building trades) doing such work are bound too; only the main builders are coded here.

confidence_note: The law's own words require building or plumbing work to comply with the code. Drafted on 27 November 2026 for the NCC work (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N3); the variation counts are from the NCC 2025 dataset.

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume One) as the ACT applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
